Words I like;
Clean water isn't a luxury. It's the baseline your body was built for.
Ever notice how your skin feels tight and itchy right after a shower, like you need lotion before the towel even hits the floor? That's not your soap. That's hard water.
Here's what's actually happening. Hard water is loaded with calcium and magnesium. When those minerals hit your soap, they don't rinse clean. They bind together and leave a film, kind of like the ring you see around a bathtub. Except now that film is sitting on your skin.
That film clogs pores, strips the natural oils your skin uses to stay soft, and throws off your skin's protective barrier. For folks with eczema or sensitive skin, it makes flare-ups worse. Kids feel it fastest, because their skin is thinner.
Soft water rinses clean. No film, no residue. Your natural oils stay put, and your skin does what it's supposed to do on its own.
If you already softened your water, that itchy tight feeling you used to fight every winter? That's the problem you paid to solve, and it stayed solved.

# Competitor Intel Brief — 2026-08-18

Only 3 of the 8 promised competitor snapshots were actually included in the context (Mermaid Water, EcoWater, Hampton Roads Water Services). The other 5 are missing. I'll brief on what's here and flag the gap.

# Section 1 — Executive Summary

The most notable competitive signal this week is the aggressive, stacked promotional activity from Mermaid Water (our most direct NoVA rival), which is now running four simultaneous offers ($200 off water heaters, $100 off first service, free Kinetico install, free heater flush) alongside a bundled water-treatment + plumbing model that widens their share of wallet. EcoWater leans on brand scale (near-century of expertise, third-party certification, smart-home leak/conservation tech) rather than price, while Hampton Roads competes on a "Lifetime Warranty" and free-water-test hook across the Hampton Roads/Richmond corridor. No competitor is publishing hard system prices—everyone gates cost behind a free in-home test, which is the industry norm and an opening for transparency. Note: only 3 of the 8 promised snapshots were delivered, so this brief is partial.

# Section 2 — Per-competitor table

| Competitor | Hero positioning (one phrase) | Distinct services | Pricing visible? | Notable shift this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mermaid Water | "Clean water + dependable plumbing from a local team that tests first" | Water treatment + full plumbing (heaters, drains, pumps, well/septic), commercial DI/RO | No hard prices; 4 promo offers ($200, $100, free install, free flush) | Heavy stacked-offer merchandising; Kinetico dealer angle emphasized (prior snapshot identical—no text diff) |
| EcoWater | "Better water starts here — global leader, backed by ~a century" | Softeners, filtration, smart-home leak/water-conservation tech | No; free water test only | No change vs. prior (identical title/meta); smart-home solutions still featured |
| Hampton Roads Water Services | "Full-service water quality experts — peace of mind" | Water + air treatment, annual water-test program, USA-made systems | No; free water test hook | No prior text to compare; leads with Lifetime Warranty + annual-test recurring touchpoint |

# Section 3 — Implications for ClearWave

- **Counter Mermaid's offer stack:** They're winning attention with 4 concurrent promos and a treatment+plumbing bundle. Test a single, clearer ClearWave offer (e.g., "$0 install + free water test") and consider whether we can credibly cross-sell plumbing/pump work to match their share-of-wallet play.
- **Borrow the recurring-revenue hook:** Hampton Roads' "Book Your Annual Water Test" turns a one-time test into a yearly touchpoint. Test an annual water-test membership/reminder program to drive retention and re-quote opportunities.
- **Exploit the pricing-opacity gap:** Nobody shows prices. Pilot even light price transparency (starting-at ranges or financing math) as a differentiator for high-intent shoppers who are tired of "book a consult to find out."

# Section 4 — Watch items

- **Missing 5 competitors** — get the remaining snapshots re-pulled; this week's landscape read is incomplete.
- **Mermaid** — watch whether the 4 offers persist, rotate, or escalate; if they become permanent, they're a structural margin bet we should price against. Check if they add published pricing.
- **EcoWater smart-home line** — leak-detection/conservation tech is a potential new front; watch for a dealer-level push in NoVA.
- **Hampton Roads** — confirm whether "Lifetime Warranty" is genuinely lifetime vs. conditional ("ask rep"); useful in head-to-head sales rebuttals. Also watch Richmond-area expansion given their dual phone lines.
